introduction: On this Sunday, Isaiah tells of the key of the house of David being placed on the shoulder of a faithful servant. In the Gospel, Peter confesses, You are the Christ, the Son of the living God, and Jesus says, You are Peter, and on this rock I will build my Church; I will give you the keys of the Kingdom of Heaven. Paul marvels at the depth of God's wisdom. Let us pray for the Pope and for the whole Church.

prayerOfTheFaithful.invitation: Brothers and sisters, Christ built his Church on the rock of Peter's faith. Let us pray for the Church and for the world.
intentions: For the Pope, successor of Peter: that the Lord may strengthen him in faith and in his service of unity. Let us pray to the Lord.
For bishops and all who hold authority in the Church: that they may use it as faithful stewards and servants. Let us pray to the Lord.
For those searching for the truth about Jesus: that the Father may reveal to them who he is. Let us pray to the Lord.
For the Church in places of persecution: that the powers of death may not prevail against her. Let us pray to the Lord.
For ourselves: that we may answer Jesus' question with our own faith: You are the Christ. Let us pray to the Lord.
prayerOfTheFaithful.conclusion: Lord God, you built your Church on the faith of Peter. Keep the Pope and all your people firm in that faith, and let the gates of death never prevail against your Church. Through Christ our Lord.

reflection.title: Who do you say that I am?
reflection.body:
In the first reading, God replaces an unfaithful steward of the royal palace with a new one, Eliakim, and gives him authority: "I will lay the key of David's house on his shoulder. He will open, and no one will shut. He will shut, and no one will open." The key is a sign of responsibility in the king's house.

In the Gospel, Jesus asks his disciples, "Who do men say that I, the Son of Man, am?" They report various opinions: John the Baptist, Elijah, Jeremiah, a prophet. Then Jesus asks the question that every Christian must answer personally: "But who do you say that I am?"

Simon Peter answers: "You are the Christ, the Son of the living God." Jesus tells him that this faith is a gift: "flesh and blood has not revealed this to you, but my Father who is in heaven." Then he gives Simon a new name and a new role: "I also tell you that you are Peter, and on this rock I will build my assembly, and the gates of Hades will not prevail against it."

Like Eliakim, Peter receives the keys: "I will give to you the keys of the Kingdom of Heaven, and whatever you bind on earth will have been bound in heaven." The Catholic Church sees in these words the foundation of the ministry of Peter and his successors, the Popes, who serve the unity of the Church in faith.

The Church is built on Christ, confessed in the faith of Peter. It is not built on human strength, and so the powers of death cannot destroy it.

Paul ends a long reflection on God's plan with wonder: "Oh the depth of the riches both of the wisdom and the knowledge of God!" Everything comes from God and returns to him.

This week, pray for the Pope by name. And answer Jesus' question in your own words: who is he for you?
